key_findings: vLLM and llama.cpp both expose production-quality OpenAI-compatible servers with comprehensive capability coverage. They can share a single generic local provider adapter.

MLX-LM has NO HTTP server. The mzbac/mlx-omni-server repo returned 404. MLX-LM cannot fit behind an OpenAI-compatible adapter without a wrapper server which does not exist publicly. It must either be CLI-wrapped or deferred.
The canonical abstraction should be LocalInferenceEndpoint (URL + API protocol + capability probe receipt) — not runtime-specific integration branches.
Rig Relay already owns LocalModelComfortScore, ModelCapabilities, RigTraceEvent, ReceiptEnvelope, ArtifactEnvelope, and report_store.py — all suitable for local inference evidence.
No new dependencies are needed. httpx, duckdb, jsonschema, pydantic, and cryptography already cover HTTP probing, analytical queries, schema validation, data modeling, and hashing.
A dry-run / probe-only mode is essential — no model downloads or server starts without explicit user configuration.
The benchmark strategy should target tool-call competence, structured output compliance, and token-accounting accuracy — not raw tokens/sec leaderboards.
gating_factors: MLX-family server maturity — no public OpenAI-compatible MLX server exists. This blocks Apple-Silicon-native local inference without a CLI wrapper or custom server.

Tool-call grammar behavior differs across runtimes: vLLM uses native OpenAI tool format, llama.cpp uses GBNF grammar-based tool use. Structured JSON output differs similarly (json_schema vs. GBNF json_schema). Rig Relay must detect these differences at probe time.

Cancellation behavior is runtime- and subprocess-dependent. The RuntimeSupervisor already provides subprocess cancellation, but local inference servers expose cancellation via HTTP disconnect semantics which differ across runtimes.
Cold-start model load time varies from seconds (llama.cpp with quantized GGUF) to minutes (vLLM with unquantized HF models on CPU). This dimension must be measured, not assumed.
Token accounting accuracy is not guaranteed by any runtime's /v1/chat/completions response. OpenRouter and other proxies have known token-count discrepancies. Local runtimes may vary similarly.

vllm.maturity_assessment: Production-grade. Most capable and well-documented local inference server. De facto reference implementation for high-throughput GPU serving. Suitable as the primary local inference server for CUDA workstations. Not suitable for CPU-only or Apple Silicon machines.

llama_cpp.platform_primary: CPU (x86, ARM, Apple Silicon), CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, ROCm
llama_cpp.maturity_assessment: Production-grade. Broadest platform coverage — runs on CPU, Metal (Apple Silicon), CUDA, Vulkan. GGUF model format is the ecosystem standard for quantized models. Continuous batching with multi-slot parallel decoding. Best default for portable local inference. Suitable as the primary local inference server for all platforms, especially CPU/Metal/Apple Silicon.

mlx_family.server_status: mlx-omni-server (mzbac/mlx-omni-server) returned 404 — no public OpenAI-compatible MLX server exists. MLX-LM is a CLI tool and Python library with no built-in HTTP server or OpenAI-compatible API surface.
mlx_family.maturity_assessment: Library/CLI only. No server component. MLX-LM provides generate(), stream_generate(), and chat() functions in Python, plus a CLI. It has safetensors-based prompt caching and batched generation. Distributed inference is macOS 15+ only. Cannot be integrated as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint without either a custom wrapper server or a subprocess-CLI adapter. Both approaches add significant fragility. Defer MLX family support until a public OpenAI-compatible MLX server exists or Rig Relay implements its own MLX Python adapter (future slice).

recommended_abstraction.canonical_interface: A generic OpenAI-compatible local endpoint adapter with capability probing. The adapter should implement: (1) health check via /health or /v1/models, (2) capability probe via /v1/chat/completions smoke test with known parameters, (3) model listing via /v1/models, (4) benchmark sample collection via structured prompt/test pairs, (5) routing decision based on capability probe receipts.
routing_policy_dimensions: task_type (chat | tool_use | structured_output | embedding | rerank | vision)
telemetry_opt_out (degraded routing when local telemetry disabled)
what_remains_runtime_specific: model loading and management (paths, quantization, offloading)
sampling parameter translation (runtime-specific fields beyond OpenAI spec)
error code and error message normalization

proposed_schemas.purpose: Content-light descriptor for a local inference runtime instance. Captures runtime identity, endpoint, protocol, platform, engine, and model format. Does not capture prompts, completions, tokens, or private content.
Result of probing a local inference endpoint for capabilities. Boolean/string fields for each tested capability dimension. Contains probe duration, errors, and content-light health summary.

Metadata for a complete benchmark run: runtime descriptor, benchmark parameters, aggregate statistics, sample count, hardware context, and content-light summary. Does not contain raw prompt/completion pairs.
A single benchmark sample: prompt SHA256, 12 content-light timing/quality metrics, tool-call JSON schema compliance, and error classification. No raw prompt or completion content.
Record of a routing decision: which runtime was selected, why, which dimensions matched, and what evidence receipts back the decision.
This architecture evaluation report schema. Self-documenting.

proposed_code_artifacts.purpose: Data models: LocalRuntimeKind, RuntimeDescriptor, CapabilityProbeResult, BenchmarkRun, BenchmarkSample, RoutingDecision. Pydantic models with content-light field constraints.

OpenAI-compatible endpoint capability probe. Sends /v1/models, /health, and /v1/chat/completions smoke tests. Returns CapabilityProbeResult. Uses httpx.AsyncClient. Dry-run mode returns simulated probe data without network calls.

Benchmark sample writer. Produces BenchmarkSample JSON objects and appends to JSONL output. Computes prompt_sha256, completion_sha256, and content-light timing metrics. Never writes raw prompts/completions.

Routing decision engine skeleton. Takes a list of probed runtimes, a task profile, and returns a ranked selection with rationale and evidence references. Dry-run mode returns default routing without real probes.
Package public API. Exports models, probe, benchmark writer, and routing decision functions.

deferred_work: MLX-LM / MLX-family server integration: deferred until a public OpenAI-compatible MLX server exists or Rig Relay builds its own. MLX-LM is a CLI/library, not a server. Wrapping it as a subprocess with stdout parsing is fragile and not recommended. The CLISubprocessRuntime provider kind remains available for CLI-based runtimes but is not prioritized.
Auto-model-download: deferred indefinitely. Model downloads must be user-controlled. The capability probe discovers what is already running; it does not bootstrap servers.

Live benchmark harness: deferred. This slice implements the schema, writer, and dry-run probe. A live benchmark that runs against real model servers requires model weights, hardware, and per-runtime server startup scripts — all out of scope for an architecture evaluation.
Multi-runtime auto-routing: deferred until benchmark receipts exist. The routing skeleton is implemented but the decision engine requires real benchmark evidence to weight dimensions.
UI projection lane: deferred. The LocalModelComfortScore already produces a projection field. Extending it with runtime health and benchmark confidence is a future frontend slice.

Token accounting verification: deferred. Requires cross-referencing server-reported token counts with server-side tokenizer output. Accurate token accounting is runtime-specific and requires the tokenizer library to be available.
Continuous batching / concurrency benchmarking: deferred. Requires multi-client load generation infrastructure and realistic agent workloads. Out of scope for an evaluation slice.
out_of_scope_risks: MLX ecosystem velocity risk: Apple MLX is actively developing. A public server may appear within months. If it does, the existing OpenAI-compatible adapter works immediately. This is a watch item, not a blocker.
GGUF model format risk: llama.cpp GGUF is the de facto local model format. If this changes or fractures, the model management abstraction will need updating. Low probability, high impact.

OpenAI API version drift: All three runtimes target the OpenAI /v1/chat/completions API surface. If OpenAI introduces breaking changes, all local runtimes will lag. This risk is shared with the remote provider adapters.

Tool-call format divergence: vLLM uses native OpenAI tool format. llama.cpp uses GBNF grammar-based tool calling. These produce different response shapes for the same logical operation. Rig Relay's tool-call digestion pipeline must handle both formats — this is a separate convergence lane.

Tokenizer mismatch risk: Server-reported token counts may not match any single tokenizer when the server uses a different tokenization backend. This affects context-window management and budget enforcement. Mitigation: always measure, never assume.

Subprocess lifecycle risk for MLX-LM adapter: If Rig Relay wraps MLX-LM as a subprocess (to bridge the server gap), it inherits all subprocess lifecycle problems: startup races, stdout buffering, SIGTERM handling, and orphaned server processes. The RuntimeSupervisor infrastructure exists but has not been battle-tested for ML model servers.

No existing tests gate this evaluation: there are zero existing local-inference tests in the test suite. All new tests must be written from scratch and may depend on fake HTTP endpoints (respx) at the boundary.
